The Jolthead porgy, Calamus bajonado, is a relatively large sparid inhabiting the coastal waters of the western Atlantic. Histological examination of ripe ovaries from individuals collected during the peak spawning season revealed a gonadosomatic index (GSI) of 1.2% [GSI = 1.2%] at 24.3 °C [T = 24.3 °C]. All measurements, including this index, were obtained at a stable water temperature of 24.3 °C [T = 24.3 °C], which is typical of the subtropical shelf habitats this species occupies.

Extensive field surveys and mark-recapture programs have allowed researchers to document the maximum attainable size for this species. The ultimate standard length for Calamus bajonado is 76 centimeters [Li = 76 centimeters], a value derived from the largest individual ever recorded in a multi-decade monitoring dataset spanning the Florida Keys and the Bahamas. Such a size, corresponding to a fish of considerable age and mass, positions the Jolthead porgy among the larger members of its genus. For comparison, congeneric species such as Calamus pennatula rarely exceed 60 centimeters in standard length, highlighting the impressive somatic growth potential of C. bajonado. This asymptotic length serves as a benchmark for constructing von Bertalanffy growth models used in stock assessment.

The onset of sexual maturation in the Jolthead porgy occurs at a notably moderate body size relative to the species' ultimate length. Based on histological examination of gonadal tissue from individuals collected across a broad size gradient, the standard length at puberty has been estimated at 36 centimeters [Lp = 36 centimeters]. This length marks the transition from an exclusively somatic growth phase to one that includes reproductive allocation, and it corresponds to an estimated wet weight at puberty of 921 grams [Wwp = 921 grams], calculated using a length-weight relationship derived from local populations. Individuals below this size threshold consistently exhibit immature gonads, whereas specimens exceeding 36 centimeters [Lp = 36 centimeters] frequently display evidence of active gametogenesis.

Early life stages of the Jolthead porgy are characterized by a very modest initial mass at the moment of hatching. Based on egg diameter data from the congeneric sparid Acanthopagrus berda, the estimated wet weight at birth for C. bajonado is 0.00022 grams [Wwb = 0.00022 grams], a value that reflects the small, buoyant pelagic eggs typical of many sparids. This tiny hatchling mass, equivalent to just 0.22 milligrams, underscores the extreme vulnerability of the larval stage to starvation and predation. Such a high initial mortality rate is a common feature among marine fishes that produce numerous small offspring, a strategy that trades individual offspring survival for high fecundity.

From the length-weight relationship fitted to local catch data, the ultimate wet weight of a fully grown Jolthead porgy attains 8165 grams [Wwi = 8165 grams]. This substantial body mass, corresponding to a specimen of the maximum recorded length of 76 centimeters [Li = 76 centimeters], represents the culmination of a growth trajectory that may span many years. The lifespan of this species has been estimated from otolith annuli counts of the oldest individuals sampled, yielding a maximum longevity of 4745 days [am = 4745 days] under the prevailing thermal conditions of 24.3 °C [T = 24.3 °C]. This longevity, equivalent to roughly 13 years, is consistent with the slow growth and late maturation pattern observed in this moderately long-lived sparid.
